_about: One lens of the public map: the outcomes of a registered QCTO qualification. This file shows which outcomes AMU's published Business Problems develop. Outcome codes and text are the qualification's own public record; the mapping is AMU's claim about its curriculum, evidenced in the governed matrices. Only outcomes developed by published Business Problems appear here; the qualification's full record lives in its module pages.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Describe the terminology and concepts used in physical asset management — in plain language, using examples from their own workplace.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Define and distinguish between the different kinds of assets — physical, fixed, movable, infrastructure, facilities — and explain how each is managed differently.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Categorise a set of assets using an identification tool — and explain the classification decisions made.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Classify physical asset types and groupings within an asset hierarchy — and justify the classification criteria used.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Discuss and demonstrate the reconciliation of assets — what it means to reconcile physical assets against the register, why it matters, and what the process involves.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Compare the characteristics of different maintenance management systems — what each is designed to do and what its limitations are.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Discuss the role of tendencies and predictions (condition monitoring, reliability data, failure patterns) in maintenance management — and why reactive maintenance is not a management system.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Discuss the practical considerations in applying a maintenance management system — what makes implementation succeed or fail in a real organisation.

nodes.label: KM-01-KT02-IAC0204
nodes.text: Evaluate physical asset maintenance management practices in their own or a described organisation — and identify specific improvements, with justification.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Assess how classification principles are applied to a described or real facilities portfolio — and identify where the application is inconsistent or incomplete.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Describe how various physical asset classification criteria are drafted — including what considerations go into designing a classification system for a specific type of organisation.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Develop classification guidelines for a set of facilities — specifying the criteria, the categories, and the decision rules for assigning each type.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Analyse how land and space interact in a facilities portfolio — including land use rights, zoning, and spatial constraints that affect what can be done with a facility.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0106
nodes.text: Discuss how sustainable development planning principles apply to the management of facilities over their lifecycle.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0107
nodes.text: Determine the specification requirements for different types of facilities — and explain how those requirements inform maintenance planning and capital investment decisions.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0108
nodes.text: Distinguish between the maintenance requirements of different facility types — explaining why the same maintenance approach does not apply equally to all facilities.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0109
nodes.text: Discuss the characteristics and properties that distinguish infrastructure assets from movable assets from immovable assets — and the management implications of each distinction.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0110
nodes.text: Evaluate the design features of various facilities and explain how design affects operability, maintainability, and compliance.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0111
nodes.text: Distinguish between different engineering environments — civil, electrical, mechanical — and the facility management implications of each.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT01-IAC0114
nodes.text: Explain the principles and concepts of property administration — including ownership records, lease management, disposal procedures, and compliance obligations.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Explain the principles of investment decision-making for physical assets — including how decisions are made, what criteria apply, and what can go wrong when the process is not followed.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Apply acquisition principles and procurement options to a described facilities acquisition — and explain the key decision points.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Discuss capital budgeting inputs for asset management — what financial information is needed to support a sound investment decision.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0207
nodes.text: Describe the principles of PMBOK project management and explain how they apply to asset creation or refurbishment projects.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0208
nodes.text: Analyse the role and composition of investment project teams — including the contributions of the asset management practitioner.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0219
nodes.text: Assess a physical asset register against minimum requirements — and identify gaps that affect compliance, accuracy, or usability.

nodes.label: KM-02-KT02-IAC0220
nodes.text: Identify and discuss the risks of further utilising an asset beyond its optimal lifecycle — including financial, safety, and compliance risks.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Describe the different lifecycle costing models in use — what each captures, what each excludes, and when each is appropriate.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Explain the key concepts and principles of lifecycle costing — including total cost of ownership, net present value at an introductory level, and the difference between capital cost and whole-of-life cost.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Apply lifecycle cost decision-making criteria to a described asset decision — identifying the full costs associated with each option and the basis for comparing them.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Describe the range of planning techniques used in asset management — long-term strategic planning, medium-term capital planning, and short-term operational planning.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Apply planning concepts and principles to a described asset portfolio — constructing a planning timeline that connects operational requirements with strategic objectives.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Explain what capital and operating budgets are and how they differ — and describe the implications for asset management of working within each type of budget constraint.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Apply the concepts and principles of various budgeting methods to asset planning — including zero-based budgeting, condition-based budgeting, and risk-based prioritisation.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Coordinate budgeting and planning for an asset portfolio — ensuring that the capital plan is grounded in the maintenance plan, which is grounded in the condition and lifecycle data.

nodes.label: KM-03-KT03-IAC0304
nodes.text: Explain the ethical dimensions of asset lifecycle decisions — including transparency, conflicts of interest, and the responsibility to provide honest analysis even when the result is unwelcome.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Evaluate the outcomes produced by applicable lifecycle costing models — assessing whether the inputs and assumptions are reasonable and whether the output supports the stated conclusion.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Explain what adherence to acceptance criteria and norms means in the context of asset performance — and identify when performance is outside acceptable bounds.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Describe what strategic planning is, what it is for, and why physical asset management must be aligned with it — not treated as a separate technical function.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Assess and value physical assets in the context of strategic planning — understanding what the asset base contributes to organisational capability and strategic objectives.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Explain the role and purpose of infrastructure assets in the context of the organisation's strategic and service delivery objectives.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0106
nodes.text: Describe the concept of integrating the physical asset management strategy with the organisational strategic plan — and identify gaps where they are currently misaligned.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0107
nodes.text: Explain governance in the context of physical asset management — including what governance structures exist, what accountability they create, and how they relate to asset management decision-making.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0111
nodes.text: Explain the concept of capacity development for asset management — and describe what it means to build an organisation's PAM capability over time.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT01-IAC0112
nodes.text: Explain business resumption planning (BRP) in the context of physical assets — and describe how it is designed and maintained.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Produce cash flow projections for an asset investment decision — including both capital outflows and operational cash flows.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Describe the investment criteria used to evaluate asset investment proposals — NPV, payback period, IRR at introductory level — and explain what each measures.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Compare the various investment options available for major asset decisions — and explain the financial and strategic trade-offs of each.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0204
nodes.text: Distinguish between capital and operating budget structures — and explain how both are managed in the context of an asset lifecycle.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0205
nodes.text: Describe service level monitoring for physical assets — what is measured, how it is reported, and what triggers a management response.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0206
nodes.text: Explain the role of call centres and centres of excellence in managing information flow across the asset management system.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT02-IAC0207
nodes.text: Describe how business information flows through the organisation in support of asset management decisions — identifying where information is lost or distorted.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Describe the statutory and fiduciary obligations relevant to physical asset management in their industry — and explain the consequence of non-compliance.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT03-IAC0302
nodes.text: Describe the PPSG framework (Policies, Procedures, Standards, and Guidelines) and explain how it creates the governance infrastructure for compliant asset management.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT03-IAC0303
nodes.text: Apply ISO 55000, SHEQ requirements, and other relevant standards to the physical asset management context — explaining what compliance requires and how it is demonstrated.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT04-IAC0401
nodes.text: Describe the role of the leader in an asset management context — and explain why effective PAM leadership often operates without formal authority.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT04-IAC0402
nodes.text: Compare different leadership styles and explain which is appropriate in different asset management situations.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT04-IAC0403
nodes.text: Describe the interpersonal skills needed to be effective in a cross-functional asset management role.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT04-IAC0404
nodes.text: Explain what makes a high-performance team in an asset management context — and describe how to build and sustain one.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT04-IAC0405
nodes.text: Describe internal development programmes (CPD) appropriate for PAM practitioners — and identify your own current development needs.

nodes.label: KM-04-KT04-IAC0406
nodes.text: Apply advanced planning principles — task planning, resource availability, workshop load management — to a complex maintenance or capital project.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Define the key terms in financial management reporting — income, expenditure, assets, liabilities, equity, depreciation, cash flow — and explain what each represents in plain language.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Explain the basic concepts and principles of financial management and reporting — including why financial reports are produced, who uses them, and what decisions they inform.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Explain the role of financial reporting in decision-making — specifically, how asset management decisions connect to financial reports and why the quality of financial data matters.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Describe the basic concepts and principles of information technology applications used in financial management — including how ERP systems integrate financial and operational data.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Explain the basic concepts of financial data analysis — what the numbers in a financial report mean and what they reveal about the financial health of an organisation.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT01-IAC0106
nodes.text: Apply financial analysis and evaluation techniques to a set of financial data — identifying what the data shows about asset-related expenditure, performance, and investment.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Define the key concepts and principles of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems — what an ERP is, what it integrates, and what it means for physical asset management.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Explain the basic principles and concepts of logistics management as they apply to physical asset management — spare parts, materials, and service contract management.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Apply the basic principles and concepts of project management to an asset management context — understanding how a capital project is tracked and managed through an ERP or project management system.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT02-IAC0204
nodes.text: Apply ERP concepts to the practical management of maintenance expenditure — understanding cost centres, GL accounts, work order cost allocation, and budget variance.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Define the key terms used in investment management and budgeting — capital expenditure, operating expenditure, payback period, net present value (introductory), return on investment.

nodes.label: KM-05-KT03-IAC0302
nodes.text: Apply the basic concepts and principles of investment management and budgeting to a real or described asset investment decision — constructing a basic business case that includes financial analysis appropriate to the decision.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Explain the methodology for producing financial reports in a maintenance and asset management context — including what data sources feed into a cost report and what process is required to ensure the report is accurate before submission.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Describe how to extract relevant financial data from an ERP for a specific cost centre, asset class, or project — including what report parameters are required and what common extraction errors produce unreliable output.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Explain the process of verifying financial data before it is reported — including cross-checking work order costs against purchase orders, goods receipts, and contractor invoices.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Describe the process of reconciling financial data — specifically how to identify and resolve discrepancies between budget and actual, between ERP records and physical activity, and between period-on-period comparisons.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Explain the structure and purpose of standard financial reporting templates used in maintenance and asset management — including period cost reports, budget versus actual reports, and asset lifecycle cost summaries.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0107
nodes.text: Explain the concept of performance reporting in a maintenance context — including how financial data combines with operational data (availability, MTBF, cost per unit output) to produce meaningful performance indicators.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0108
nodes.text: Describe the policies and procedures that govern financial reporting in an asset management organisation — including period-end close procedures, authorisation levels, and the consequences of submitting inaccurate reports.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT01-IAC0109
nodes.text: Explain the principles of Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (GAAP) as they apply to maintenance and asset management — specifically the matching principle, accruals, and the distinction between capital and operating expenditure — and describe the consequences of violating these principles in a cost report.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Describe the planning functions of an Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) or ERP system — including how planned maintenance, corrective work orders, and project work are scheduled, resourced, and costed within the system.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Explain the role of logistics management in maintenance operations — including how materials, equipment, and contractor resources are coordinated to support planned and unplanned maintenance, and how logistics decisions generate financial transactions.

nodes.label: KM-06-KT02-IAC0207
nodes.text: Explain workflow management in an ERP — how the sequence of approvals and transactions (notification → work order → purchase requisition → purchase order → goods receipt → invoice verification → cost posting) controls both the operational process and the financial data it generates — and describe what happens to financial data when a step in this workflow is executed incorrectly or out of sequence.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Apply analytical thinking and logic to evaluate the current state of an asset management system framework against its intended purpose — identifying systemic failures, not isolated data errors.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Evaluate whether the asset management system framework is integrated with the financial management system — identifying gaps that create GRAP 17 non-compliance, audit risk, or divergence between operational records and financial records.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Select and apply appropriate data gathering tools to restore currency and integrity to asset data — matching the tool (financial records review, field inspection, engineering assessment, system cross-reference) to the data type and source.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Demonstrate understanding of how data quality affects the value of management reporting — connecting specific data gaps to specific decisions, budgets, or compliance requirements that are undermined by poor data.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS01-IAC0105
nodes.text: Correctly capture and maintain physical asset data integrity — applying the defined data standard to create or correct records using verifiable, auditable data sources.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Compile a procedure to establish data standards for the asset register — defining mandatory fields, acceptable data sources, update frequency, and responsible roles.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Define asset management standards that are consistent with the organisation's asset management strategy and plans — ensuring the standard supports lifecycle decision-making, not just data compliance.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Ensure asset management standards reflect the strategic goals of the organisation — connecting the data standard to the service delivery, financial sustainability, and compliance objectives it is designed to support.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Review legislative and operational/financial requirements (GRAP 17, MFMA, Water Services Act, Blue Drop criteria) and demonstrate understanding of how these requirements shape the data collection and reporting procedures.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS03-IAC0302
nodes.text: Benchmark asset data procedures against good practice — identifying comparable organisations or standards that provide a credible reference point for the designed procedure.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS03-IAC0303
nodes.text: Develop procedures that support physical asset integration and quality, and that connect to financial reporting requirements — not isolated from the financial system.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS03-IAC0304
nodes.text: Draw a process map that reflects all elements of an integrated process — from asset acquisition through annual update to disposal, with defined triggers, responsibilities, and verification points.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS04-IAC0401
nodes.text: Draft specifications for an integrated asset management information system that encompasses all relevant elements of the asset management strategy and plans — functional requirements, financial integration, user access, reporting, and data security.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS05-IAC0501
nodes.text: Prepare a phased implementation plan based on credible best practice models — with realistic timelines, resource requirements, dependencies, and measurable success criteria for each phase.

nodes.label: PM-01-PS06-IAC0601
nodes.text: Compile a performance assessment report that integrates all aspects: current state (evidence-based), root cause analysis, proposed improvements with justification, resource requirements, and implementation priorities — coherent enough to support an executive decision.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Research and describe the operational environment systematically — documenting production requirements, utilisation rates, operating conditions, and how these drive asset demand and degradation.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Evaluate models used to understand the operational environment — selecting appropriate analytical frameworks (e.g., production capacity models, utilisation analysis, condition degradation models) and justifying their use.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Discuss operational and financial constraints with clear logic — explaining how each constraint limits the available options and affects the lifecycle decision.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS01-IAC0104
nodes.text: Develop a physical asset management plan grounded in the environmental analysis — ensuring the plan is responsive to actual operational conditions, not assumed ones.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Evaluate investment options using a 5-year total cost of ownership comparison — including capital cost, maintenance cost escalation, production loss cost, and risk cost — and produce a recommendation with supporting analysis.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Research and apply an appropriate performance modelling approach — documenting the methodology, data sources, and assumptions clearly enough that another person could reproduce the model.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS03-IAC0302
nodes.text: Apply statistical thinking to performance data — distinguishing trends from anomalies, identifying correlation between variables (e.g., age and maintenance cost, operating hours and failure rate), and avoiding common analytical errors (extrapolation beyond data range, ignoring sample size).

nodes.label: PM-02-PS03-IAC0303
nodes.text: Apply mathematical accuracy in performance calculations — calculating availability, MTBF, MTTR, and cost ratios correctly, showing workings, and identifying what each metric measures and what it does not.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS04-IAC0401
nodes.text: Evaluate and select an appropriate maintenance strategy model — justifying the choice of preventive, predictive, condition-based, or RCM approach for each asset cohort based on failure modes, criticality, and cost.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS04-IAC0402
nodes.text: Evaluate the assumptions underlying the strategy — identifying which assumptions are data-supported and which are estimates, and describing the sensitivity of the strategy to errors in each assumption.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS04-IAC0403
nodes.text: Demonstrate the process of arriving at a final strategy recommendation — showing the trade-offs considered and explaining why the chosen approach is preferred over the alternatives.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS04-IAC0404
nodes.text: Demonstrate logical and analytical thinking throughout the strategy development process — producing a coherent rationale that connects the asset's failure modes to the selected maintenance tasks.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS05-IAC0501
nodes.text: Apply RCM (Reliability-Centred Maintenance) fundamentals — identifying functional failures, failure modes, and effects for the key assets in the scenario; selecting appropriate maintenance tasks based on failure consequence.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS05-IAC0502
nodes.text: Apply risk estimation techniques — rating likelihood and consequence, calculating risk scores, and explaining the basis for each rating with sufficient specificity to be challenged by a reviewer.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS05-IAC0503
nodes.text: Align the maintenance task list with the competence level of the available workforce — identifying where capability gaps exist and how they will be addressed (training, contracting, or task redesign).

nodes.label: PM-02-PS06-IAC0601
nodes.text: Evaluate the risk assessment in the context of applicable SLAs and contracts — identifying where contractual coverage reduces risk and where gaps in contractual protection expose the organisation.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS06-IAC0602
nodes.text: Evaluate the appropriateness of mitigation measures in an SLA — identifying whether response time requirements, penalty mechanisms, and reporting obligations are adequate to protect the organisation's performance targets.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS07-IAC0701
nodes.text: Evaluate negotiation outcomes and specifications — assessing whether the contractual arrangements reached in supplier negotiations adequately protect the organisation's interests.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS07-IAC0702
nodes.text: Evaluate the data and information used in drafting specifications — ensuring specifications are based on verifiable performance data and realistic benchmarks, not aspirational figures.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS07-IAC0703
nodes.text: Evaluate the alignment of specifications and plans with organisational policies, procurement regulations, and governance requirements.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS08-IAC0801
nodes.text: Produce a physical asset management lifecycle plan that integrates all prior analysis — investment recommendation, performance forecast, maintenance strategy, risk register, SLA requirements, and decision triggers.

nodes.label: PM-02-PS08-IAC0802
nodes.text: Produce a schedule of maintenance actions — specific, resourced, and time-bounded — that implements the maintenance strategy for the first planning period.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Research and produce a report on physical asset system trends — using a structured methodology that is explicitly documented, reproducible, and connects performance data to management implications.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Apply statistical thinking to performance data — distinguishing trends from anomalies, identifying the period over which a trend is significant, and avoiding common errors (treating a single data point as a trend, ignoring seasonality, extrapolating beyond the data range).

nodes.label: PM-03-PS01-IAC0103
nodes.text: Apply mathematical accuracy to performance calculations — calculating KPIs (availability, MTBF, MTTR, planned maintenance completion rate, cost ratios) correctly, showing workings, and connecting each metric to the management question it answers.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Conduct a supplier performance assessment — comparing actual performance against SLA targets across multiple periods, calculating any applicable penalties, and documenting specific remediation requirements with measurable milestones.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Identify and manage critical products and services — defining which supplier relationships are critical to the organisation's asset performance and what level of monitoring and engagement is appropriate for each criticality tier.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Apply the organisation's monitoring and evaluation framework to interpret performance results against the established baseline — categorising systems as within baseline, approaching threshold, or in breach; distinguishing between systems that require immediate action, monitoring, and investigation.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS04-IAC0401
nodes.text: Evaluate the organisation's physical asset management plan against specific statutory legislation — identifying which legislative obligations apply, what the prescribed requirements are, and whether current practice meets those requirements.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS04-IAC0402
nodes.text: Review a set of statutory compliance records and comment on compliance status — identifying specific breaches, calculating the duration of non-compliance, assessing the regulatory consequence, and recommending remedial action with appropriate urgency and escalation level.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS05-IAC0501
nodes.text: Draft an operational performance report using appropriate data — drawing on M&E framework results, supplier assessments, compliance reviews, and financial data to produce an integrated picture that supports decision-making rather than merely describing events.

nodes.label: PM-03-PS05-IAC0502
nodes.text: Ensure the operational performance report aligns with organisational requirements — structured to enable the decision-makers who receive it to act on its findings; distinguishing clearly between what requires their decision and what has already been managed.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Identify the operational and maintenance requirements that must be reflected in a new asset specification — including maintainability, spare parts availability, operator training requirements, and compatibility with existing asset management systems and processes.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Evaluate a new asset specification against operational and maintenance requirements — identifying gaps, conflicts with existing systems, or provisions that would impose unacceptable lifecycle costs, and proposing specific amendments with clear rationale.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Conduct a structured pre-commissioning check to verify that a new asset meets its specification, that all documentation is present, and that the asset is ready to be handed over for operational use — using a systematic checklist methodology.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Identify and formally document non-conformances or outstanding items discovered during the pre-commissioning check — recording the nature of the non-conformance, its location, its potential consequence, and the action required to close it.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Evaluate the risk of proceeding to commissioning or operation with outstanding non-conformances — distinguishing between items that are acceptable to leave for post-commissioning resolution and items that must be closed before operation can proceed.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Prepare the asset management documentation required to support the handover of a new asset to operations — including asset register entries, maintenance plans, spare parts provisioning, operating procedures, and as-built documentation.

nodes.label: PM-04-PS03-IAC0302
nodes.text: Assess the readiness of the receiving organisation to operate and maintain the new asset — confirming that operators have been trained, that maintenance resources and spares are in place, and that the organisation can support the asset from day one of operation.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS01-IAC0101
nodes.text: Identify which statutory legislation imposes reporting obligations on the organisation in relation to its physical assets — distinguishing between operational performance reports, asset condition reports, and financial performance reports, and naming the specific legislation and regulatory body for each obligation.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS01-IAC0102
nodes.text: Define the specific requirements for each statutory reporting obligation — what data must be reported, in what prescribed format, at what frequency, by what deadline, and to which regulatory authority — and confirm where prescribed templates or submission portals apply.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS02-IAC0201
nodes.text: Identify the internal data sources required for each statutory reporting obligation — confirming that each source is current, authoritative, and has been verified against the underlying records — and flagging any sources that are incomplete, inconsistent, or of uncertain reliability.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS02-IAC0202
nodes.text: Compile and format performance data in accordance with prescribed reporting requirements — using the regulator's prescribed units, definitions, calculation methods, and format — and confirming that compiled data matches the verified source records.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS02-IAC0203
nodes.text: Identify and resolve data gaps or discrepancies discovered during compilation — documenting what was found, what was done to resolve it, and whether any residual gaps must be disclosed in the submission or escalated before submission.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS03-IAC0301
nodes.text: Review a draft statutory report against the prescribed requirements — checking that all required sections are present, all mandatory fields are completed, all calculations are correct, and all data references match the underlying source records.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS03-IAC0302
nodes.text: Identify and formally document errors, omissions, or inconsistencies in a draft statutory report — specifying what is wrong, where it appears, what the correct information is, and what must be done before the report can be submitted.

nodes.label: PM-05-PS04-IAC0401
